title: Max out your HSA if you have an HDHP
summary: The only triple-tax-advantaged account in the U.S. system. Treat it as a stealth retirement account, not a healthcare slush fund.
detailsHtml:
Why the HSA goes before the IRA

An IRA contribution avoids tax at either contribution (Traditional) or withdrawal (Roth) — never both. An HSA avoids tax at three points: pre-tax contribution, tax-free growth, and tax-free qualified withdrawal. The compounded effect over 30+ years is meaningful.

2026 HSA limits: $4,400 self-only coverage $8,750 family coverage +$1,000 catch-up at age 55+ (not 50)

The stealth retirement strategy

Pay current medical expenses out of pocket. Keep the receipts. Invest the HSA balance in low-cost equity index funds. Decades later, you can reimburse yourself from the HSA for the original expenses — having let the funds compound tax-free in the meantime. After age 65, HSA withdrawals for non-medical purposes are taxed like a Traditional IRA (ordinary income, no penalty), so worst case it functions like another Traditional account.

HSA jurisdictional quirks: California and New Jersey do not recognize HSA contributions as tax-deductible at the state level. The federal benefits still apply, but the math is slightly worse for residents of those states.
